mainTopic: When a כהן's daughter may eat תרומה and מעשר after her marriages, and the limits on her return to her father's house: חזה ושוק, a widow awaiting יבום, and a pregnant woman.
overview: The משנה follows a כהן's daughter through marriages to a ישראל, a לוי and a כהן. It rules at each stage whether she may eat תרומה or מעשר, depending on her husband or a living son from him. When all the children who block her are gone, she returns to her father's house and eats תרומה again. The גמרא finds the source for going back to eating because of a son in the extra word ״וּבַת״. Even the רבנן agree, because the whole word is extra. A ברייתא limits her return: she eats תרומה again but not חזה ושוק. Five אמוראים each give a different פסוק source for this, and רבא defends one of them against a challenge about vows. A second ברייתא says a woman who eats because of her son goes back even to חזה ושוק, and רב אשי explains why she gets more than the כהן's own daughter. Finally, the גמרא excludes a widow awaiting יבום and a pregnant woman, and shows why ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ and ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ are both needed. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A כהן's daughter through three marriages
steps.stepSummary: The משנה traces a כהן's daughter who marries a ישראל, then a לוי, then a כהן. It rules at each stage whether she may eat תרומה or מעשר, even after the husband dies and a son from him is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן's daughter married to a ישראל may not eat תרומה. If he died and she has a son from him, she still may not eat תרומה. If she then married a לוי, she may eat מעשר. If he died and she has a son from him, she may still eat מעשר. If she then married a כהן, she may eat תרומה. If he died and she has a son from him, she may still eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out a chain of marriages. It tells us what holy food the woman may eat at each stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her eating rights follow her current husband. If he dies, they follow a living son from that husband. A son from a ישראל keeps her from going back to her father's תרומה. A son from a לוי or a כהן keeps her eating at that family's level.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to a כהן; only כהנים and their households may eat it
The tithe given to a לוי
She married
And she has a son from him

steps.confusionAlert: Even after a husband dies, a living son from him keeps her tied to that husband's status. That is why the son matters so much in every line.

phrases.aramaic: בַּת כֹּהֵן שֶׁנִּיסֵּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל — לֹא תֹּאכַל בִּתְרוּמָה.
phrases.english: A kohen's daughter who married a Yisrael may not eat teruma.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת וְלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ בֵּן — לֹא תֹּאכַל בִּתְרוּמָה.
phrases.english: If he died and she has a son from him, she may not eat teruma.
If she married a Levi, she may eat maaser.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת וְלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ בֵּן — תֹּאכַל בְּמַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: If he died and she has a son from him, she may eat maaser.
If she married a kohen, she may eat teruma.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת וְלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ בֵּן — תֹּאכַל בִּתְרוּמָה.
phrases.english: If he died and she has a son from him, she may eat teruma.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her right to eat תרומה or מעשר follows her current husband, or a living son from him after the husband dies.

steps.title: As each son dies, she falls back a level
steps.stepSummary: The משנה now has the sons die one by one. Each death removes the rights that son gave her. When the son from the ישראל dies, she returns to her father's house and eats תרומה, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her son from the כהן died, she may not eat תרומה. If her son from the לוי died, she may not eat מעשר. If her son from the ישראל died, she goes back to her father's house. About her the פסוק says: 'And she returns to her father's house as in her youth; she may eat of her father's bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה runs the chain backwards. It shows what happens as each son dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the son from the כהן gone, she drops to the level the son from the לוי gives her, which is מעשר. With that son gone too, the son from the ישראל still blocks her from her father's תרומה. Once he also dies, nothing blocks her, so she goes back to her father's תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: She returns to her father's house, meaning she gets back her right to eat תרומה as a כהן's daughter
As in her youth
She may eat of her father's bread, meaning his תרומה

steps.whatToRemember: A living child from a non-כהן blocks a כהן's daughter from her father's תרומה. A living child from a כהן lets her eat תרומה. Once all the blocking children are gone, she goes back to her father's house.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת בְּנָהּ מִכֹּהֵן — לֹא תֹּאכַל בִּתְרוּמָה.
phrases.english: If her son from the kohen died, she may not eat teruma.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת בְּנָהּ מִלֵּוִי — לֹא תֹּאכַל בְּמַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: If her son from the Levi died, she may not eat maaser.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת בְּנָהּ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל — חוֹזֶרֶת לְבֵית אָבִיהָ,
phrases.english: If her son from the Yisrael died, she returns to her father's house,
and about this woman it is said:
"And she returns to her father's house as in her youth;
she may eat of her father's bread."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same case, now as the sons die one by one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As each son dies she loses the rights he gave her. When the son from the ישראל dies, she goes back to eating her father's תרומה.

steps.title: Where do we learn she goes back to eating because of her son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up the case of a woman who eats תרומה once her marriage to a לוי has ended. She can do so because of her son from a כהן. It asks for the source that a son can bring her back to eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'If her son from the לוי died, she may eat תרומה.' This rule, that she goes back to eating because of her son, where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the rule and asks for its source in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a woman who had a son from a כהן and then married a לוי. While she was married to the לוי, she could not eat תרומה. Once that link ends, she goes back to eating תרומה because of her son from the כהן. The גמרא wants to know how we know a son can bring her back to תרומה like this.

keyTerms.meaning: That she goes back and eats
Because of her son
From where do we know it?

steps.confusionAlert: These words are not a word-for-word line from the משנה above. The גמרא is pulling out a rule that follows from how the משנה's cases work.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ מֵת בְּנָהּ מִלֵּוִי — תֹּאכַל בִּתְרוּמָה.
phrases.english: GEMARA: If her son from the Levi died, she may eat teruma.
phrases.notes: She can eat תרומה here because she still has a living son from an earlier marriage to a כהן.

phrases.english: That she goes back to eating because of her son, from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the תורה source of a rule that comes out of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק source showing that a son from a כהן brings his mother back to eating תרומה after a marriage to a non-כהן has ended.

steps.title: רב learns it from the extra word ״וּבַת״
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes רב: the פסוק could have said ״בַּת״ but says ״וּבַת״. The extra wording adds this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב: it could have said 'בַּת' (a daughter), yet it says 'וּבַת' (and a daughter).
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. He points to the extra word in the פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא 22:13 begins ״וּבַת כֹּהֵן״ instead of just ״בַּת כֹּהֵן״. That extra wording is read as adding a case. It is the source for a woman going back to eating תרומה because of her son from a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A daughter' versus 'and a daughter': the extra 'and' is the source

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav said:
"Daughter" — "and daughter."
phrases.notes: The פסוק in ויקרא 22:13 could have just said ״בַּת״, but it says ״וּבַת״, so something extra is being added.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra wording ״וּבַת״ in ויקרא 22:13 adds the case of going back to eating תרומה because of a son.

steps.title: Does this only work for רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view this is. Learning from an extra ו׳ is the method of רבי עקיבא. So does רב's source only work for him?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? Is it like רבי עקיבא, who learns from an extra ו׳?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how wide רב's proof reaches. It suggests the proof may only fit one תנא's way of reading פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learns new rules from a single extra letter ו׳. The רבנן usually do not. If רב's source is just an extra ו׳, it would seem to hold only for רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose view is this?
Who learns from extra ו׳ letters

phrases.english: Like whom? Like Rabbi Akiva, who expounds extra vavs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far רב's proof from ״וּבַת״ reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב's proof only works for רבי עקיבא, who learns from an extra ו׳.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the proof rests only on an extra ו׳, it would be rejected by the רבנן, who do not learn from extra ו׳ letters.

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree: the whole word is extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even the רבנן accept this proof. Here not just the letter ו׳ but the entire word ״וּבַת״ is extra, because the previous פסוק already mentioned a כהן's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the רבנן: the whole word 'וּבַת' is an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the proof works for everyone, not only for רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן only refuse to learn from a lone extra letter. Here the whole word ״וּבַת״ could have been left out, since the earlier פסוק already spoke of a כהן's daughter. An entire extra word is something even the רבנן learn from.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the רבנן
An extra, unneeded word in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The source for a woman going back to eating תרומה because of her son from a כהן is the extra word ״וּבַת״. Since the whole word is extra, everyone agrees, not only רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows the Rabbis,
since the entire word "and daughter" is an extra word in the verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5, so רב's proof stands for everyone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widens the proof: an entire extra word, not just a letter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof rests on an extra ו׳ alone, so only רבי עקיבא would accept it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole word ״וּבַת״ is extra, so even the רבנן accept the proof.

steps.title: She returns to eating תרומה but not to חזה ושוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא limits how far her return goes: she gets back תרומה, but not the breast and thigh of קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: When she returns to her father's house, she goes back to eating תרומה. She does not go back to eating the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a limit to the woman who returns to her father's house: she eats תרומה again, but not חזה ושוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we learned that she goes back to eating תרומה. This ברייתא says the return is only partial: the portions of קרבנות given to the כהן are not given back to her. The next steps look for the source.

keyTerms.meaning: She returns.
The breast and right thigh of a שלמים, given to the כהן

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
When she returns, she returns to eating teruma,
but she does not return to eating the breast and thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the return to her father's house described in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A returning כהן's daughter eats תרומה but not חזה ושוק.

steps.title: First source: the words ״בתרומת הקדשים״
steps.stepSummary: רבינא בר שילא learns the rule from the פסוק that forbids her the portion lifted off from קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רבינא בר שילא: What is the פסוק? "She may not eat of the set-apart portion of the holy things." This means she may not eat what is lifted off from the holy offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא בר שילא gives a פסוק as the source for the ברייתא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads ״תרומת הקדשים״ as "what is lifted off from the קרבנות", and that means חזה ושוק. The פסוק's ban on these portions stays in place even after she returns home.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק? (asking for the source)
The portion set apart from holy offerings
What is lifted off and separated from the קרבן for the כהן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Ravina bar Sheila said:
What is the verse?
"She may not eat of the set-apart portion of the holy things,"
meaning: from what is lifted off from the holy offerings she may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״בתרומת הקדשים לא תאכל״ forbids her the lifted-off portions, which are חזה ושוק.

steps.title: Second source: ״מלחם״ means only some bread
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה learns the rule from the ״מ״ in ״מלחם״: some of her father's food, not all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: "Of bread" means not all bread. This excludes the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different source for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says she eats ״מלחם״, "from" her father's bread, and not just ״לחם״. The word "from" means "some of". So not everything a כהן eats goes back to her, and חזה ושוק are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: From the bread, meaning some of it
To exclude

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
"Of bread" means not all bread,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:13. The extra ״מ״ is read as "some of".

phrases.english: which excludes the breast and thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: מִלֶּחֶם וְלֹא כׇּל לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second source for the same rule

steps.title: Maybe ״מלחם״ excludes cancelling her vows
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks why ״מלחם״ must teach about חזה ושוק. Perhaps it teaches that her father cannot cancel her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא challenged this: Why not say it excludes the cancelling of vows?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא attacks רב נחמן's reading. The "some, not all" might point to a different exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״מלחם״ only shows that she does not fully return to her youth, any limit could fit. It might mean her father loses the power to cancel her vows. Then nothing would be left to teach about חזה ושוק.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it
Cancelling vows, which a father can do for his young daughter

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama challenged this:
Say instead that it excludes the cancelling of vows!
phrases.notes: He means: she goes back to her father, but he can no longer cancel her vows the way he could when she was young.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exclusion is open-ended. It could just as easily refer to vow cancellation as to חזה ושוק.

steps.title: Vows are already taught by דבי רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a ברייתא from דבי רבי ישמעאל already teaches that the father cannot cancel her vows. So ״מלחם״ is free to teach about חזה ושוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The school of רבי ישמעאל already cut her off from her father on this point. They taught: "But the vow of a widow or a divorcee shall stand upon her."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his answer to רמי בר חמא. He points to a ברייתא that already handles vows, and the next steps explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If another source already teaches that the father cannot cancel her vows, ״מלחם״ is not needed for that. So רב נחמן can use it for חזה ושוק.

keyTerms.meaning: He already cut it off, meaning the matter is already decided
A teaching from the study house of רבי ישמעאל
Shall stand upon her, meaning the vow stays in force

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר פַּסְקַהּ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: The tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael already cut it off,
for the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"But the vow of a widow or a divorcee
shall stand upon her,"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּבָר פַּסְקַהּ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר חמא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: The other proposed reading is already covered by a separate source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״מלחם״ might be needed to teach that her father cannot cancel her vows
steps.terutzMaskana: Vows are covered by במדבר 30:10, so ״מלחם״ teaches חזה ושוק

steps.title: Why does the Torah need this פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק is needed. A widow or divorcee is obviously no longer under her father or her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the פסוק need to say this? She is already out of her father's authority and out of her husband's authority!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, the תנא asks what the פסוק adds. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow or divorcee has no husband, and she left her father's control when she married. So of course no one can cancel her vows, and the פסוק seems unnecessary. The answer will show that it teaches a special case.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
Taken out of the category of

phrases.english: Why does the verse need to say this?
Isn't she already out of the father's category,
and out of the husband's category!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא questions the need for the פסוק it just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point the פסוק about a widow's or divorcee's vows teaches

steps.title: Widowed on the way: once out of her father's authority, always out
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches a case where she was handed to the husband's agents and was widowed or divorced on the way. Since she left her father's authority even for a moment, he can never cancel her vows again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where the father, or the father's agents, handed her over to the husband's agents, and she was widowed or divorced on the way. Is she in her father's house or her husband's house? The פסוק teaches that once she left her father's authority for one moment, he can no longer cancel her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with an in-between case. This finishes רבא's proof that vows are already covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case she never reached her husband's home, so one might think she is still under her father. The פסוק says no: one moment outside his authority ends his power to cancel her vows. So the vow law is already taught here, and ״מלחם״ is free to exclude חזה ושוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband's agents
The father's authority
One moment

steps.whatToRemember: Once a daughter leaves her father's authority through marriage, even for a moment, he can never again cancel her vows. That is why רמי בר חמא's reading of ״מלחם״ is not needed, and רב נחמן's source stands.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, הֲרֵי שֶׁמָּסַר הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: Rather, take a case where the father handed her over to the husband's agents,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁמָּסְרוּ שְׁלוּחֵי הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: or the father's agents handed her over to the husband's agents,
and she was widowed or divorced on the way,
how should I regard her?
Is she in her father's house,
or in her husband's house?
Rather, the verse comes to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצְאָה שָׁעָה אַחַת מֵרְשׁוּת הָאָב —
phrases.english: once she left her father's authority for even one moment,
he can no longer cancel her vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הֲרֵי שֶׁמָּסַר הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question and completes רבא's answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק covers a bride widowed or divorced on the way. One moment out of her father's authority ends his power to cancel her vows.

steps.title: Third source: bread, not meat
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא reads ״לחם״ literally. She eats bread-type gifts like תרומה, but not meat like חזה ושוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: "Of her father's bread she may eat" means bread, and not meat.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא gives another reading of the same פסוק to exclude חזה ושוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא does not need the extra ״מ״. The word ״לחם״ itself shows the limit: grain-based תרומה comes back to her, but meat portions of קרבנות do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread, and not meat

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
"Of her father's bread she may eat" means
bread, and not meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָפְרָא אָמַר: מִלֶּחֶם אָבִיהָ תֹּאכֵל, לֶחֶם וְלֹא בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another source after the challenge to רב נחמן was settled
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״לחם״ includes bread-type gifts and excludes the meat of חזה ושוק.

steps.title: Fourth source: bread her father owns
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reads ״לחם אביה״ as food her father owns. כהנים do not own חזה ושוק; they eat them from ה׳'s table.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: "Of her father's bread she may eat" means bread that her father owns. This excludes the breast and thigh, because the כהנים receive them from the table of the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth אמורא reads ״אביה״ as "belonging to her father", which leaves out חזה ושוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה becomes the כהן's own property, so it counts as her father's bread. חזה ושוק never truly belong to the כהן. He eats them as a guest at ה׳'s table, so they are not "her father's" and she cannot share them.

keyTerms.meaning: Owned by her father
The table of the Most High, meaning ה׳'s table
They receive or acquire

steps.whatToRemember: So far there are four sources for why a returning כהן's daughter eats תרומה but not חזה ושוק: ״בתרומת הקדשים״, the ״מ״ of ״מלחם״, ״לחם״ and not meat, and ״לחם אביה״ as food her father owns. The next step adds a fifth.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
"Of her father's bread she may eat" means
bread that is owned by her father,
which excludes the breast and thigh,
because they receive them from the table of the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מִלֶּחֶם אָבִיהָ תֹּאכֵל, לֶחֶם הַקָּנוּי לְאָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a fourth source for the same rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She eats only what her father owns. חזה ושוק are received from ה׳'s table and are not owned by the כהן.

steps.title: רבא's source: daughters eat the breast and thigh only while they are 'with you'
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from ״אִתָּךְ״ in ויקרא 10:14 that a כהן's daughter eats חזה ושוק only while she is still part of his household, not after she returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: 'And the breast of waving and the thigh of lifting you shall eat, you and your sons and your daughters with you.' This means: at a time when she is with you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own source that a returning בת כהן does not go back to eating חזה ושוק. He uses the word ״אִתָּךְ״ (with you).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק allows daughters to eat חזה ושוק only while they are 'with you', meaning still in their father's house. Once she married a ישראל and left, she is no longer 'with you', even if she later comes back. This is a different source from the four given in the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The breast of the waving: the breast of a שלמים offering, given to the כהן
The thigh of the lifting: the right thigh of a שלמים offering, given to the כהן
With you, meaning still part of your household
At a time when, only while

phrases.english: And Rava said:
"And the breast of waving
and the thigh of heaving
you shall eat, you and your sons
and your daughters with you"
at a time when she is with you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fifth source, after those of רבינא בר שילא, רבה בר אבוה, רב ספרא and רב פפא, for the rule that a returning בת כהן does not eat חזה ושוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daughters eat חזה ושוק only while they are 'with' their father, still in his household.
steps.whatToRemember: There are five sources for why a returning כהן's daughter eats תרומה but not חזה ושוק: ״בתרומת הקדשים״ (רבינא בר שילא), the ״מ״ of ״מלחם״ (רבה בר אבוה), ״לחם״ and not meat (רב ספרא), ״לחם אביה״ as food her father owns (רב פפא), and ״אִתָּךְ״ (רבא).

steps.title: A ברייתא: she returns to תרומה but not to breast and thigh, while a woman eating because of her son returns even to them
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה quotes a ברייתא: a returning בת כהן eats תרומה again but not חזה ושוק. A woman who ate because of her son from a כהן goes back even to חזה ושוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said that a ברייתא taught: When she returns to her father's house, she returns to eating תרומה, but she does not return to eating חזה ושוק. If she ate because of her son, she returns even to חזה ושוק.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא is brought that states outright what the earlier sources learned from the פסוקים. It then adds a new case: a woman who ate because of her son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half confirms the rule: the returning בת כהן gets back תרומה only. The second half is new. A ישראלית who ate because of her son from a כהן, then married a ישראל who died, gets back both תרומה and חזה ושוק. This surprising difference sets up רב אשי's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: She returns, goes back to eating
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Because of her son: she eats through her son from a כהן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, תָּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said, it was taught:
When she returns to her father's house,
she returns to eating teruma,
but she does not return to the breast and thigh.
If she ate because of her son,
phrases.notes: This is a ישראלית with a son from a כהן. She later married a ישראל, and he died.

phrases.english: she returns even to the breast and thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the rule from the earlier sources with a ברייתא and adds a new contrasting case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A returning בת כהן eats תרומה but not חזה ושוק. A woman who ate because of her son returns even to חזה ושוק.

steps.title: רב אשי asks: how can the son's mother get more than the כהן's own daughter?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks: the woman eating because of her son is learned from ״וּבַת״, the פסוק about the כהן's daughter. How can she be better off than the daughter herself?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי went and said this teaching in front of רב אשי. רב אשי said: From where is she included? From ״וּבַת״. Is she better than the one she is learned from?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is brought to רב אשי, and he challenges its second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right of a woman with a son from a כהן to go back to eating comes from the same פסוק as the returning בת כהן. Normally a case learned from another case cannot be stronger than its source. So how can she return to חזה ושוק when the בת כהן cannot?

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching, a halachic statement
Is included, learned from an extra word
Is she better? A challenging question

phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai went
and said the teaching before Rav Ashi.
He said: From where is she included?
From "And a daughter"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:13, the פסוק about the כהן's daughter coming back home.

phrases.english: Is she better than the one she comes from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a woman eating because of her son returns even to חזה ושוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her right is learned from the בת כהן's פסוק, so she should not get more than the בת כהן herself.

steps.title: Answer: only the כהן's daughter has limiting words written about her
steps.stepSummary: For the בת כהן the Torah wrote limiting words. For the woman eating because of her son it did not, so she returns fully.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, limiting words are written. Here, limiting words are not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אשי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בת כהן is kept from חזה ושוק only because the Torah added special limiting words (like ״מִלֶּחֶם״ and ״אִתָּךְ״). Those limits were said about her alone. The woman eating because of her son is learned from the basic rule of returning, without those limits, so she goes back to everything.

keyTerms.meaning: Limiting words in a פסוק that exclude something
There / here: comparing two cases

steps.whatToRemember: A returning בת כהן eats תרומה but not חזה ושוק because of special limiting words. A woman eating because of her son has no such limits, so she returns to both.

phrases.english: There, exclusions are written,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the כהן's daughter. The limiting words are the ones from the earlier steps, like ״מִלֶּחֶם״ and ״אִתָּךְ״.

phrases.english: here, exclusions are not written.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם כְּתִיבִי מִיעוּטֵי, הָכָא לָא כְּתִיבִי מִיעוּטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two cases by what is written in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A case learned from the בת כהן cannot have more rights than she has.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limits on the בת כהן come from extra words said only about her, so they do not carry over to the woman eating because of her son.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a widow awaiting יבום and a pregnant woman do not count as 'returning'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes a ברייתא: ״וְשָׁבָה אֶל בֵּית אָבִיהָ״ leaves out a שומרת יבם, and ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ leaves out a pregnant woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A כהן's daughter who married a ישראל, and so on. The רבנן taught: 'And she returns to her father's house' leaves out a widow waiting for her יבם. 'As in her youth' leaves out a pregnant woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the line in the משנה about a בת כהן married to a ישראל. It brings a ברייתא that learns two cases from the פסוק of her returning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For her to eat תרומה again, she has to truly return to her father's house. A שומרת יבם is still tied to her husband's family, so she has not really returned. ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ means she is as she was before marriage, and a pregnant woman is not, so she also cannot eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the rest of the משנה line is assumed
This leaves out, excludes
A widow waiting for her husband's brother to do יבום
A pregnant woman

phrases.english: A priest's daughter who married an Israelite, etc.
The Sages taught:
"And she returns to her father's house"
excludes a widow awaiting her yavam.
"As in her youth"
excludes a pregnant woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת כֹּהֵן שֶׁנִּיסֵּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חזה ושוק discussion and goes back to the משנה to learn more details from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומרת יבם and a pregnant woman do not return to eating תרומה.

steps.title: Can't we learn the pregnant woman rule by logic?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the need for ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ by building a קל וחומר from יבום to תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do we need a פסוק? Use logic: by יבום, the Torah does not count a child from the first husband the way it counts a child from the second husband, and still it treats an unborn baby like a born one. By תרומה, the Torah does count a child from the first husband like one from the second. Surely there it should also treat an unborn baby like a born one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed the word ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ to exclude a pregnant woman. It suggests we could figure it out by logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By יבום, only a child from the husband who died exempts the widow, yet even an unborn child exempts her. By תרומה, a child from any Israelite husband keeps the בת כהן from eating, which is a broader rule. So the argument says that if the narrower area counts an unborn child, the broader area surely should too.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it a logical argument? (opens a קל וחומר)
A fetus, an unborn baby
A child who has already been born
Marriage of a childless widow to her husband's brother
To disqualify her

phrases.english: But is it not a logical inference?
If in a place where [the Torah] did not make

phrases.aramaic: וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי
phrases.english: a child from the first husband like a child from the second husband
to exempt her from יבום,
it still made a fetus like a born child,
then in a place where it did make a child from the first husband

phrases.aramaic: כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי לְפוֹסְלָהּ מִן הַתְּרוּמָה —
phrases.english: like a child from the second husband to disqualify her from תרומה,
is it not logical that we should make a fetus like a born child?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the derivation ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ — פרט למעוברת quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ to exclude a pregnant woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from יבום (narrower about which children count) to תרומה (broader about which children count) should already teach that a fetus counts, so the פסוק seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The logic fails: יבום has a stricter rule
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is rejected because by יבום even a child who died still counts, which is not true by תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Maybe יבום counts an unborn baby like a born one because יבום also counts a dead child like a living one. Should we say the same for תרומה, where a dead child does not count like a living one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the logical argument from the last step. It shows that יבום has a special stricter side, so we cannot learn תרומה from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By יבום, if the widow had a child when her husband died, she is exempt even if the child later died, so a dead child counts like a living one. By תרומה, once her child dies she may eat again, so a dead child does not count. Since יבום is stricter in this way, maybe that is why it also counts a fetus, and תרומה might not.

keyTerms.meaning: So what? That proves nothing for here (rejects a comparison)
With regard to, in the matter of
Treating the dead like the living

phrases.aramaic: לָא, מָה לִי עָשָׂה עוּבָּר כְּיָלוּד
phrases.english: No; what does it prove that it made a fetus like a born child
regarding יבום,
since there it made the dead like the living?
phrases.notes: A child alive when the husband died exempts the widow from יבום even if the child later dies.

phrases.english: Shall we make a fetus like a born child regarding תרומה,
where it did not make the dead like the living?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מָה לִי עָשָׂה עוּבָּר כְּיָלוּד לְעִנְיַן יִיבּוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר proposed in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר from יבום to תרומה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: יבום has a stricter feature (a dead child counts like a living one) that תרומה lacks, so its rule about a fetus may come from that strictness and cannot be carried over.

steps.title: So the פסוק ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ is needed
steps.stepSummary: Since logic fails, the פסוק ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ is needed to teach that a pregnant woman does not return to תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״, to leave out a pregnant woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes this back-and-forth: because the logic didn't work, the Torah had to write ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's teaching from step 20 is now justified. A pregnant woman is not like she was in her youth, so she does not go back to eating תרומה, and we only know this from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק teaches
As in her youth (ויקרא 22:13)
A pregnant woman

steps.whatToRemember: A pregnant בת כהן widow does not return to תרומה, and this comes from the word ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״, not from logic, because יבום is stricter than תרומה.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: “As in her youth” —
to exclude a pregnant woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logic is rejected in step 22, it returns to the פסוק as the real source.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The exclusion of a pregnant woman from returning to תרומה needs the פסוק ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״, since it cannot be learned from יבום.

steps.title: Why both פסוקים are needed: part one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ alone would not teach the pregnant woman case, because she is still only one body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah had to write both the pregnant woman rule and ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״. If it wrote only ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״, I would say: she can't eat because at first she was one body and now she comes back as two. But a pregnant woman was one body then and is still one body now, so I might say she may eat. So the extra teaching is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why the Torah needed two separate teachings: one about a woman with a child, and one about a pregnant woman. This step gives the first half of the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who returns with a born child is clearly different from her youth, since there are now two separate people. A pregnant woman still looks like one person, so without ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ we might let her eat. That is why the pregnant woman rule had to be written.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
And she has no child (ויקרא 22:13)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Body, a separate person
It is needed (both teachings are necessary)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two teachings: ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ is about a child already born, and ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ is the source for a pregnant woman.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write the case of a pregnant woman,
and it was necessary to write “and she has no child.”
For if the Merciful One had written only “and she has no child,”
I would say: at the start she was one body
and now there are two bodies,
but a pregnant woman,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא חַד גּוּפָא וְהַשְׁתָּא חַד גּוּפָא —
phrases.english: who at the start was one body and now is still one body,
I might say she may eat; so it is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב מְעוּבֶּרֶת, וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having shown that ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ is needed, the גמרא explains why ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ does not make it unnecessary.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ alone would not exclude a pregnant woman, since she is still one body; so the pregnant woman rule had to be written.

steps.title: Why both פסוקים are needed: part two begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts the second half: if only the pregnant woman rule were written, there would be a reason not to apply it to a woman with a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Merciful One had written only the pregnant woman case, I would say that is because at the start her body...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the opposite side of the reasoning: why the pregnant woman rule alone would not be enough. The sentence continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the reason that ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ is also needed. Here the גמרא only starts comparing her body at the start with her body now, and the full reason follows next.

keyTerms.meaning: And if
At the start, originally

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only the pregnant woman,
I would say it is because at the start her body…

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of the explanation started in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Begins explaining why the pregnant woman rule alone would not teach the case of a woman with a born child.
